task: Fix the four confirmed backend attack paths
status: Four findings fixed locally; prepared migration and deployment-host acceptance remain.

fixes.behavior: Mandatory authenticated large uploads validate the same current_player dependency before body delivery or parser admission. Missing/invalid sessions return 401 without receive(). Explicit test dependency overrides use the real FastAPI dependency resolver; no production bypass was added. Valid credentials are checked every request and again at the endpoint after body delivery, with the existing player budget charged only once.
fixes.isolation: Public discovery has a separate one-slot pool; product telemetry retains its existing separate pool. An anonymous discovery slow body cannot occupy race/publication upload slots. Unknown routes receive only the small 32 KiB control allowance.

fixes.behavior: The boundary resolves a declared route and rejects unsupported methods with 405/Allow before receiving/decompressing/parsing a body. Bodyless read routes reject payloads. Every allowed large body takes a parser lease independent of HTTP method, held through validation, handler and response. Existing small control writes may still send {}.
fixes.compatibility: Cheap declared-length bounds remain before authentication; correlated headers and safe route-template logs remain. The publication gzip-limit test now supplies a valid session, keeping its original 413 assertion. The privacy-of-logs test expects 405 for an unsupported POST rather than reaching its previous content-type rejection; all correlation/non-echo assertions remain.

fixes.behavior: An owner-locked durable reservation, containing immutable owner/key/body/hash identity, precedes object IO. Canonical bytes and retained intent/upload counts are bounded across replicas. Partial storage/DB failures and process loss keep their charge and references. Matching deliveries reuse one reservation and immutable objects. Replacement leases fence old writers; a failed old writer cannot clear a replacement lease. A successful short transaction transfers the charge to the queued intent and removes the reservation atomically.
fixes.identity: The server-owned creator snapshot survives profile changes during incomplete-upload recovery. Contract field types/lengths are bounded before storage, preventing uncharged large contract JSON. Known intent retries remain owner/body-bound and do not need new allowance.
fixes.retention: Bounded retention retires old terminal rejected evidence and expired incomplete reservations. Small permanent operation-key/request-hash tombstones prevent replaying retired operations. Published content/creator proof references and retryable validator/build/entitlement failures remain protected. GC references include live upload reservations and exclude retired evidence; online pins and stopped-writer offline rules remain.
fixes.migration: 0033 adds reservation/retirement accounting and conservatively charges legacy nonpublished intents at their former 512 KiB document + 2 MiB replay bound. Tests downgrade to the prior schema, seed legacy records and verify upgrade preservation/accounting.

fixes.behavior: Identical fresh queries coalesce within the short refresh window. Identical query/order vectors also share one persisted snapshot per lifetime bucket across refresh windows and replicas; changed order retains a separate immutable cursor. Alias hints are capped at 64, and the existing vector RAM bound remains.
fixes.limits: A shared locked database budget caps stored version IDs and snapshot rows, including empty-result variants. SQL result materialization is capped; over-cap catalogues receive an explicit 503 rather than a silently incomplete listing. Bounded expiry cleanup releases budget atomically. Cache/cursor hits remain usable when creation allowance is full. A separate per-validated-player or trusted-peer creation budget prevents repeated query variants from consuming the whole creation pool.
fixes.migration: 0033 backfills actual legacy snapshot lengths and initializes shared counters. The database budget lock serializes duplicate first creation and quota admission across replicas.

operational_defaults.notes: Hosting limits, tunable after traffic acceptance. Publication allowance covers incomplete/queued/failed evidence, not successful published content or legitimate racing. Logical canonical bytes are charged conservatively per operation; physical disk/WAL/provider usage is not claimed to equal these values. Terminal evidence uses the existing retention window (default 90 days).

validation_notes: Counts are per invocation and overlap; do not sum them as unique tests.

The final broad isolated SQLite run passed 289 tests, with nine row-lock/OS skips and 166 deselections. The old trajectory-less full-replay rewind fixture remains unchanged and excluded as documented in the review.

The broader PostgreSQL stage passed 63 tests with four skips; it includes real API/worker processes, recovery and locking. The final affected PostgreSQL suite passed 33 with three SQLite-parameter skips after snapshot refinement/migration coverage.

The final merged workspace focused run passed 58 checks while concurrent account privacy work was present. Broad/PG/POSIX checks used committed complete backend code plus task-owned changes, excluding that unfinished feature. Validation hashes record the exact snapshot.

Initial Windows loopback database connections timed out with and without sandbox escalation. PostgreSQL was reached directly inside an existing disposable Linux network namespace. No timeout assertion was weakened.

Intermediate runs encountered concurrent missing account columns/imports, not a security fix failure. Complete source isolation preserved the workspace edits. The unrelated owner.deleted_at publication guard and privacy settings are excluded only from the isolated task patch/test snapshot, not from the workspace.

The first Linux backup wrapper run could not execute its generated mock Docker script on the temporary mount; the isolated test container was rerun with an executable /tmp. The helper assertions and application scripts were unchanged.

An initial broad run showed an unintended 400 for a nonexistent grant endpoint; small unknown/control writes were restored to their original bounded behavior, keeping the original 404 grant denial assertion.
Ruff, scoped git diff --check and secure-environment pip check passed. No dependency was added or installed.
